why: run_accounting_health_across in tools_cross_instance.py only fans out read-only fetch_aging_lines/search_read calls across instances resolved via select_instances(), which is bounded to the operator-configured instance allowlist (cross_instance.py select_instances/parse_instances_meta); no caller-controlled host/URL escapes that list.

tools_accounting.py's accounting_health_summary takes only an optional instance name (validated against configured instances) and forwards to build_unreconciled_summary, which issues read-only search_count/search_read calls; no caller-controlled sink beyond the caller's own Odoo account.

run_aggregate_across (tools_cross_instance.py) validates model via validate_model_name, parses measures via parse_measure_spec's fixed aggregator allowlist, applies field_policy.check_aggregate per instance, and only queries instances from the configured allowlist via select_instances; the read_group call is forwarded to the caller's own Odoo instance.

tools_read.py's aggregate_records validates the model name, parses each measure through parse_measure_spec's fixed aggregator allowlist, blocks denied fields via field_policy.check_aggregate, and forwards group_by/domain/measures to the caller's own Odoo server via odoo.execute_method(read_group/formatted_read_group); domain itself is normalized through normalize_domain_input which uses ast.literal_eval/json.loads, never eval, so there is no local injection surface.

analyze_upgrade_log_report (diagnostics.py) only takes log_text as a string, truncates it to MAX_LOG_BYTES, and regex-matches each line against a fixed, bounded pattern list (patterns use small {0,80} quantifiers); it never opens a file path, never contacts Odoo, and never executes anything derived from the text.

build_domain_report (agent_tools.py) only validates conditions against SAFE_DOMAIN_OPERATORS and optional fields_metadata and returns the constructed domain list; it never executes the domain against Odoo or anywhere else.

business_pack_report (tools_diagnostics.py) uses the caller-supplied 'pack' string only to select a static bucket in build_business_pack_report; when use_live_metadata is true it only calls read-only odoo.get_models()/get_installed_modules(), never a write or arbitrary method.

cancel_async_task only cancels a pending/running entry in the process-wide AsyncTaskManager by task_id (task_queue.py); this server's design gives every caller the same underlying Odoo service-account identity per instance (credentials are configured server-side per instance, not per MCP caller), so there is no distinct principal being denied authorization here any more than the bare-stdio/no-transport-auth property the task explicitly excludes from per-tool findings; task_id is a 48-bit uuid4 hex, not sequential.

sink: odoo.execute_method(model, "message_post", [record_id], **canonical["kwargs"]) — executes immediately once the supplied approval.token string-matches a value computed purely from the caller's own request fields
guard: bypassable: token is odoo-write:sha256(canonical_json(payload))[:32] (agent_tools.build_approval_token) with no server secret and no session-side registration (unlike preview_write/validate_write, chatter_post never calls register_write_approval/require_validated_write_approval). A caller can compute the identical hash from the exact model/record_id/body/message_type/subtype_xmlid/partner_ids/attachment_ids/instance it is about to send and pass approval={'token': <that hash>}, confirm=true on the very first call, fully skipping the 'preview first' step the tool's own description promises ('Default mode requires an approval token returned from a preview call').
why: The tool's declared safety contract is a two-step preview-then-confirm gate for a DESTRUCTIVE_TOOL, but the 'approval' is only a deterministic hash of caller-controlled fields with no secret or server-side state, so it authorizes nothing beyond what the caller already asserted about its own request. This is a real, concretely-demonstrated bypass of the tool's own stated authorization gate, contrasted directly with the properly session-registered gate used by preview_write/validate_write/execute_approved_write in the same file.
contract: Default mode requires an approval token returned from a preview call; set MCP_CHATTER_DIRECT=1 to bypass and post immediately.

why: data_quality_report (tools_data_quality.py) validates model name, clamps sample_limit, and delegates to build_data_quality_report which only issues search_read/search_count/execute_method('search',...) read-only calls; relation 'target' models for the orphan check come from Odoo's own fields_get metadata (meta['relation']), not caller input.

diagnose_access (tools_diagnostics.py) explicitly documents and implements read-only metadata/count calls only (search_read on ir.model, context_get, search_count) with no sudo/impersonation; domain/record_ids are normalized the same safe way as search_records and forwarded to the caller's own Odoo account.

diagnose_odoo_call_report (diagnostics.py) is a pure input-driven classifier over model/method/args/kwargs/metadata; it never calls odoo.execute_method or any network/file API, matching its 'without executing it' description which we verified in the code rather than trusting the docstring alone.

_execute_approved_write_gated (tools_write.py) requires verify_write_approval to match, then require_validated_write_approval(app_context, approval) to find a non-expired record that was only created by a prior validate_write call in this same server session (server_core.register_write_approval/require_validated_write_approval, TTL-bound), then re-checks write_approval_payload equality, confirm=true, and writes_enabled(); a caller cannot forge entry into app_context.write_approvals merely by computing the token hash, unlike chatter_post.

excerpt: if method in READ_ONLY_METHODS or method.startswith(("get_", "_get_")):
sink: odoo.execute_method(model, method, *args, **kwargs) in tools_write.py execute_method — runs whatever method name passed classify_method_safety with caller-supplied args/kwargs
guard: partial: classify_method_safety() (diagnostics.py) is a pure name-based heuristic; DESTRUCTIVE_METHODS (create/write/unlink) are hard-blocked and SIDE_EFFECT_METHOD_PATTERNS/'unknown' methods require an explicit allowlist entry or ODOO_MCP_ALLOW_UNKNOWN_METHODS, but any existing Odoo/addon method merely named starting with 'get_' or '_get_' is classified 'read_only' (even at only medium confidence) and is exempt from that review gate entirely.
why: If the connected Odoo instance has any custom method (a real possibility in third-party addons, which are not part of this repo) named with a get_/_get_ prefix that nonetheless performs a write or side effect, execute_method will run it with caller-supplied args/kwargs without ever requiring policy-file/env allowlisting, purely because of the name heuristic. We could not confirm from this repo's own code whether such a method exists on any real target instance, so this stays Tier B rather than A.
contract: Odoo model method to call; direct create, write, and unlink are blocked.

why: build_fit_gap_report (diagnostics.py) only classifies caller-supplied requirements/available_models/available_fields/installed_modules into static buckets; it never contacts Odoo or any other sink even when use_live_metadata is set (the tool only appends an info-level note, it does not fetch anything).

generate_json2_payload_report (diagnostics.py) only string-formats an endpoint path/URL and JSON body preview; it never issues an HTTP request (confirmed by reading the function body, which does no urllib/requests call), matching the 'without network access' description.

get_async_task only polls AsyncTaskManager.status(task_id) in the process-wide task store; as with cancel_async_task, every caller of this server shares the same underlying Odoo service-account identity per configured instance, so there is no distinct-privilege boundary being crossed by reading another call's task result within one process, and task_id (uuid4 hex[:12]) is not guessable/sequential.

get_model_fields validates the model name, forwards to odoo.get_model_fields (a read-only fields_get), applies field_policy redaction markers, and only reorders/filters the returned dict locally; no execution or injection surface.

get_odoo_profile returns url/hostname/db/username/transport/verify_ssl/server_version/user_context/installed_modules — no password or API key field is ever included (confirmed by reading the exact dict built in tools_read.py), so there is no credential exposure, and the rest is a read-only forward to the caller's own instance.
health_check takes no arguments and only reports locally computed posture (surface counts, rate_report(), plugin_posture(), runtime_security_report()); there is no caller-controlled input to trace.

index_knowledge validates the model name, normalizes domain safely, fetches via read-only odoo.search_read, applies field_policy.redact_records before indexing, and stores documents purely in an in-process BM25 dict (knowledge_index.py) — there is no filesystem path derived from caller input anywhere in this path.
inspect_model_relationships_report only reads/uses fields_get-shaped metadata (caller-supplied or fetched read-only) to compute relationship/required-field summaries; no write or execution path.
knowledge_stats takes no arguments and only returns get_knowledge_store().stats(), a local in-memory summary of index sizes.

list_async_tasks takes no caller-controlled arguments and returns only name/status/timestamps for tasks (never the result payload, per TaskRecord.snapshot(include_result=False)); no sensitive data or sink is reachable through this tool.

list_instances takes no arguments and list_configured_instances() (odoo_client.py) builds its summary from an explicit key allowlist (url/db/transport/is_default/tags/cross_instance) that never copies username/password, so there is no credential exposure and no caller-controlled input to trace.

list_models forwards to read-only odoo.get_models() and filters the returned list locally in Python using a caller-supplied substring query; the substring is never sent back to Odoo as part of a domain, so there is no injection surface.

lookup_model_history_report (agent_tools.py) only looks the caller-supplied name string up in a static, curated rename/removal catalog baked into the source; it never contacts Odoo or executes anything, matching its 'static and never contacts Odoo' description which we verified in the code.

preview_write only builds a canonical approval-token report via build_write_preview_report; it validates model name and operation shape but never calls odoo.execute_method or otherwise mutates Odoo state — actual execution only happens later through execute_approved_write's separate, session-gated path.

read_attachment only takes an integer attachment_id (validated > 0) and reads ir.attachment fields/datas via odoo.execute_method('ir.attachment','read',...) against the caller's own Odoo server — it never opens a local filesystem path, so there is no path-traversal surface despite the name suggesting file access.

read_record validates model name and record_id>0, resolves a safe field list via resolve_read_fields, and forwards to odoo.read_records — a straightforward read-only ORM call to the caller's own instance, with field_policy redaction applied on the result.

receivable_payable_aging validates direction against a fixed 2-value set, clamps limit/top_partners, and delegates to build_direction_aging/fetch_aging_lines which only issue read-only search_read calls against account.move.line on the caller's own instance.

scan_addons_source passes addons_paths through restrict_addons_paths (server_core.py), which resolves each candidate path (Path.resolve, following symlinks and normalizing '..') and rejects any path not equal to or contained within an operator-configured ODOO_ADDONS_PATHS root, raising if no roots are configured at all; the scan loop itself also skips symlinked files. This closes the traversal path a caller-supplied addons_paths could otherwise attempt (e.g. '../../etc').

schema_catalog validates model names, caches by a JSON key of its own inputs, and only calls read-only odoo.get_models()/get_model_fields(); caller-controlled 'query' is only used for a local substring filter, never forwarded as an Odoo domain.

run_search_across validates model name, normalizes domain safely, and resolves the 'instances' selector through select_instances() which is bounded to the operator's configured instance list (cross_instance.py); each worker's search_read is a read-only call to that caller-selected-but-allowlisted instance.

search_employee forwards the caller's 'name' string as the 'name' kwarg of Odoo's own hr.employee.name_search method via odoo.execute_method — a fixed method/model with no locally-interpreted injection surface; the search semantics are entirely Odoo server-side.

search_holidays validates start_date/end_date with strptime (rejecting non-YYYY-MM-DD input), builds a domain list of Odoo [field, operator, value] leaves (values are plain strings/ints passed as domain terms, not concatenated into any query string), and forwards to read-only odoo.search_read.

search_knowledge validates the model name and only queries the local in-process BM25 KnowledgeStore.search(); it 'never contacts Odoo' (verified in code — no odoo client is even resolved in this tool), and the query string is only tokenized locally, never interpreted as code or a path.

search_records validates model name, normalizes domain via normalize_domain_input (json.loads/ast.literal_eval, never eval, with strict shape validation rejecting anything it can't fully parse), clamps limit, and forwards to read-only odoo.search_read on the caller's own instance, with field_policy redaction applied to results.

submit_async_task dispatches on the caller-supplied 'operation' string through a closed if/elif chain against fixed literals (never getattr/eval/dynamic lookup) in tools_async.py; each branch builds its job through the same validated per-tool helpers (restrict_addons_paths, validate_model_name, normalize_domain_input) already reviewed as clear/guarded for their synchronous counterparts, and writes are explicitly never accepted here.

build_upgrade_risk_report (diagnostics.py) only classifies caller-supplied module/method/source_findings/observed_errors data against static rule tables; it is input-driven and never calls odoo.execute_method even when use_live_metadata is set (that flag only appends an informational note), matching the 'without executing Odoo calls' description which we verified in the code.

validate_write only reads live model metadata via odoo.get_model_fields (read-only) and, when that succeeds, registers a server-side approval record (register_write_approval); it never itself calls create/write/unlink — actual execution requires the separately-gated execute_approved_write path.
